decisions.reason: The word is the master who owns a slave, used of God (meaning decisions m1, m3). "Bwana" is the owner of a slave in Swahili; "Mkuu" keeps this title apart from "Bwana" for the Lord, which the chapter uses throughout.

source.text: ὅτι εἶδον οἱ ὀφθαλμοί μου τὸ σωτήριόν σου ὃ ἡτοίμασας κατὰ πρόσωπον πάντων τῶν λαῶν, φῶς εἰς ἀποκάλυψιν ἐθνῶν καὶ δόξαν λαοῦ σου Ἰσραήλ.

records.literal_gloss: Because saw the eyes of me the salvation of you \v 31 which you prepared before [the] face of all the peoples, \v 32 a light for revelation of Gentiles and glory of [the] people of you Israel.

en.L: because my eyes have seen {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation, \v 31 which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have prepared before [the] face of all the peoples, \v 32 a light for revelation to [the] Gentiles and glory to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel."
en.B: because my eyes have seen the salvation that comes from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \v 31 which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have prepared in full view of every people: \v 32 a light of revelation for the nations, and the glory of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel."
en.R: With my own eyes I have seen the one {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent to save us. \v 31 You have prepared {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for all people to see. \v 32 He will be a light to show the truth to people who are not Jews, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring glory to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel."

es.L: porque mis ojos vieron {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} salvación, \v 31 la que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} preparaste ante [la] faz de todos los pueblos, \v 32 luz para revelación a [los] gentiles y gloria de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo Israel».
es.B: porque mis ojos han visto la salvación que viene de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, \v 31 la que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has preparado a la vista de todos los pueblos: \v 32 luz de revelación para las naciones, y gloria de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo Israel».
es.R: Con mis propios ojos he visto al que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} enviaste para salvarnos. \v 31 Tú {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} has preparado a la vista de todos los pueblos. \v 32 Él será una luz que mostrará la verdad a los que no son judíos, y traerá gloria a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo Israel».

fr.L: car mes yeux ont vu {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} salut, \v 31 que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as préparé devant la face de tous les peuples, \v 32 lumière pour la révélation aux nations et gloire de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple Israël. »
fr.B: car mes yeux ont vu le salut qui vient de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, \v 31 que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as préparé sous le regard de tous les peuples : \v 32 une lumière qui se révèle aux nations, et la gloire de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple Israël. »
fr.R: De mes propres yeux, j’ai vu celui que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as envoyé pour nous sauver. \v 31 Tu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}as préparé pour que tous les peuples {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voient. \v 32 Il sera une lumière qui fera connaître la vérité aux non-Juifs, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} apportera la gloire à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple Israël. »

sw.L: kwa sababu macho yangu yameshuhudia wokovu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, \v 31 ulioutayarisha mbele ya uso wa jamii zote za watu, \v 32 nuru ya ufunuo kwa watu wa mataifa, na utukufu wa watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} Israeli."
sw.B: kwa kuwa kwa macho yangu nimeuona wokovu utokao {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}, \v 31 ambao umeuandaa mbele ya watu wa kila taifa, waone: \v 32 nuru ya ufunuo kwa mataifa, na utukufu wa watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} Israeli."
sw.R: Kwa macho yangu mwenyewe nimemwona yule uliyemtuma ili atuokoe. \v 31 Umemwandaa ili watu wote wamwone. \v 32 Yeye atakuwa nuru ya kuwaonyesha ukweli watu wasio Wayahudi, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atauletea utukufu watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} Israeli."

decisions.choice: your salvation: the child, in whom God's saving work has come
alternatives: salvation in general, apart from the child
decisions.reason: Simeon holds the child and says he has seen God's salvation. The noun is a related form of the key word "salvation", used in Isaiah 40:5 ("all flesh shall see the salvation of God", quoted in Luke 3:6).

decisions.choice: a light for the Gentiles: Isaiah 42:6; 49:6; 52:10
decisions.reason: God says of his servant, "I will make you a light for the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth" (Isaiah 49:6). Isaiah 52:10 adds that all the nations will see God's salvation. Simeon says the child is that light for the nations, and Israel's glory.

decisions.choice: a light for revelation to the Gentiles and glory to Israel: two things the salvation is
alternatives: light for both, and glory for both
decisions.reason: Both nouns stand in apposition to "your salvation". The light reveals God to the nations; the glory belongs to Israel, from whom the Savior comes. Some read "glory" as a second thing the light brings.

decisions.choice: Gentiles: the nations, people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: The word means the nations as distinct from Israel.

decisions.choice: the one you sent to save us
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the salvation Simeon sees is the child.

decisions.choice: the nations
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the plain word; Readable explains it.

decisions.choice: los gentiles (L); las naciones (B); los que no son judíos (R)
decisions.reason: The terms used through Luke for the nations who are not Israel (meaning decision m4); Readable says who they are, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: les nations (L, B); les non-Juifs (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet (style guide 9) has it, following the English per level: Literal and Balanced say "nations", Readable says who they are. "Païens" now suggests unbelief or idolatry rather than simply not being Jewish.

decisions.choice: watu wa mataifa (L); mataifa (B); watu wasio Wayahudi (R)
decisions.reason: The terms used through Luke for the nations who are not Israel (meaning decision m4); Readable says who they are, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἦν ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ θαυμάζοντες ἐπὶ τοῖς λαλουμένοις περὶ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And was the father of him and the mother marveling at the things being spoken concerning him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} father and mother were marveling at the things being said about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: His father and mother stood amazed at what was being said about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus's father and mother were amazed at what Simeon said about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} padre y la madre estaban maravillados de las cosas que se decían acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Su padre y su madre estaban asombrados de lo que se decía de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: El padre y la madre de Jesús estaban asombrados de lo que Simeón decía de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} père et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère s’étonnaient de ce qui était dit à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sujet.
fr.B: Son père et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère restaient émerveillés de ce qu’on disait de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Le père et la mère de Jésus étaient très étonnés de ce que Siméon disait de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Na baba {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na mama walikuwa wakistaajabia mambo yaliyokuwa yakisemwa kuhusu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}.
sw.B: Baba {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} walishangazwa na yale yaliyosemwa kuhusu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}.
sw.R: Baba na mama wa Yesu walishangaa kwa yale ambayo Simeoni alisema kuhusu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}.

decisions.choice: his father, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Joseph, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts have "Joseph and his mother", perhaps to protect the virgin birth. Luke himself calls Joseph and Mary "his parents" (2:27, 41) and has Mary say "your father" (2:48). Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: his father: Joseph, his legal father
decisions.reason: Luke has told of the virgin birth (1:34-35) and says Jesus was thought to be Joseph's son (3:23). Joseph is his father in law and in the care he gives.

source.text: καὶ εὐλόγησεν αὐτοὺς Συμεὼν καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς Μαριὰμ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ· Ἰδοὺ οὗτος κεῖται εἰς πτῶσιν καὶ ἀνάστασιν πολλῶν ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ καὶ εἰς σημεῖον ἀντιλεγόμενον, καὶ σοῦ δὲ αὐτῆς τὴν ψυχὴν διελεύσεται ῥομφαία, ὅπως ἂν ἀποκαλυφθῶσιν ἐκ πολλῶν καρδιῶν διαλογισμοί.

records.literal_gloss: And blessed them Simeon and said to Mary the mother of him, Behold this is appointed for fall and rising of many in the Israel and for a sign being spoken against, \v 35 and of you and yourself the soul will go through a sword, so that may be revealed from many hearts thoughts.

en.L: And Simeon blessed them and said to Mary {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother, "Look, this [child] is appointed for [the] falling and rising of many in Israel, and for a sign that is spoken against \v 35 (and a sword will pierce through your own soul too), so that [the] thoughts of many hearts may be revealed."
en.B: Then Simeon blessed them and said to Mary, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother, "This child is set to make many in Israel fall and rise again. He will be a sign that people oppose, \v 35 and a sword will go through your own soul as well, so that the thoughts of many hearts will come to light."
en.R: Simeon asked God to bless them. Then he said to Mary, the mother of Jesus, "God has chosen this child to cause many people in Israel to fall and many to rise. He will be a sign from God, but many people will speak against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 35 And your own heart will feel pain, as if a sword had cut into it. Because of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the secret thoughts of many people will be shown."

es.L: Y Simeón los bendijo y dijo a María, {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre: «Mira, este [niño] está destinado a [la] caída y [al] levantamiento de muchos en Israel, y a ser señal que provoca oposición \v 35 (y a ti también una espada te atravesará el alma), a fin de que queden al descubierto [los] pensamientos de muchos corazones».
es.B: Luego Simeón los bendijo y dijo a María, {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre: «Este niño está puesto para que muchos en Israel caigan y vuelvan a levantarse. Será una señal a la que la gente se opondrá, \v 35 y a ti misma una espada te atravesará el alma; así saldrán a la luz los pensamientos de muchos corazones».
es.R: Simeón pidió a Dios que los bendijera. Después dijo a María, la madre de Jesús: «Dios ha elegido a este niño para hacer que muchos en Israel caigan y que muchos se levanten. Será una señal de Dios, pero mucha gente hablará en contra de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. \v 35 Y tu propio corazón sentirá dolor, como si una espada lo atravesara. Por causa de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se conocerán los pensamientos secretos de muchas personas».

fr.L: Et Siméon les bénit et dit à Marie, {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère : « Voici, celui-ci est établi pour la chute et le relèvement de beaucoup en Israël, et pour un signe qu’on contredit \v 35 (et ton âme à toi aussi, une épée la traversera), afin que les pensées de beaucoup de cœurs soient dévoilées. »
fr.B: Puis Siméon les bénit et dit à Marie, {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère : « Cet enfant est là pour faire tomber et relever beaucoup de gens en Israël. Il sera un signe auquel on s’opposera, \v 35 et une épée transpercera ton âme à toi aussi, afin que les pensées de bien des cœurs soient mises au jour. »
fr.R: Siméon a demandé à Dieu de les bénir. Puis il a dit à Marie, la mère de Jésus : « Dieu a choisi cet enfant pour faire tomber beaucoup de gens en Israël, et pour en relever beaucoup d’autres. Il sera un signe venu de Dieu, mais beaucoup de gens parleront contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. \v 35 Et toi, ton cœur souffrira beaucoup, comme si une épée le transperçait. À cause de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, les pensées secrètes de beaucoup de gens seront dévoilées. »

sw.L: Na Simeoni akawabariki, akamwambia Mariamu mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, "Tazama, [mtoto] huyu ameteuliwa ili wengi katika Israeli waanguke na kuinuka, na awe ishara ambayo watu wataipinga \v 35 (nawe, upanga utapenya nafsi yako mwenyewe pia), ili mawazo ya mioyo mingi yafichuliwe."
sw.B: Kisha Simeoni akawabariki, akamwambia Mariamu, mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, "Mtoto huyu amewekwa ili wengi katika Israeli waanguke na kuinuka tena. Atakuwa ishara ambayo watu wataipinga, \v 35 na upanga utachoma nafsi yako mwenyewe pia, ili mawazo ya mioyo mingi yawekwe wazi."
sw.R: Simeoni akamwomba Mungu awabariki. Kisha akamwambia Mariamu, mama wa Yesu, "Mungu amemchagua mtoto huyu ili kusababisha watu wengi katika Israeli waanguke na wengi wainuke. Atakuwa ishara kutoka kwa Mungu, lakini watu wengi watasema maneno ya kumpinga. \v 35 Na moyo wako mwenyewe utaumia, kana kwamba upanga umeuchoma. Kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, mawazo ya siri ya watu wengi yataonekana wazi."

decisions.choice: the falling and rising of many: the stone that makes some stumble, Isaiah 8:14-15; 28:16
alternatives: the same people falling and then rising
decisions.reason: God will be a stone that makes many in Israel stumble and fall (Isaiah 8:14-15), and a tested cornerstone for those who trust (28:16). Jesus applies the stone texts to himself (20:17-18). Some in Israel will fall because they reject him; others will rise. It may also be the same people, humbled and then raised (1:52).

decisions.choice: a sign spoken against: a sign from God that people will oppose
decisions.reason: The child will point to God, as a sign does, but many will reject him, as Luke's story goes on to show.

decisions.choice: a sword will pierce your soul: Mary's deep grief, above all at her son's rejection and death
decisions.reason: The large sword is a picture of piercing pain. The words stand as an aside to Mary in the middle of the sentence: the opposition to her son will cut through her too.

decisions.choice: so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed: the purpose of the sign and the opposition
decisions.reason: The clause goes back to the sign spoken against: how people respond to Jesus shows what is in their hearts.

decisions.choice: the aside about the sword kept in its place (B); placed before the purpose clause as its own sentence (R)
alternatives: moved to the end, as one more prophecy
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the Greek order with commas instead of parentheses. Readable gives each part its own sentence.

decisions.choice: your own heart will feel pain, as if a sword had cut into it
alternatives: a sword will pierce your soul
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means and keeps the sword.

decisions.choice: asked God to bless them
decisions.reason: To bless someone is to ask God's good for them.

source.text: Καὶ ἦν Ἅννα προφῆτις, θυγάτηρ Φανουήλ, ἐκ φυλῆς Ἀσήρ αὕτη προβεβηκυῖα ἐν ἡμέραις πολλαῖς, ζήσασα μετὰ ἀνδρὸς ἔτη ἑπτὰ ἀπὸ τῆς παρθενίας αὐτῆς, καὶ αὐτὴ χήρα ἕως ἐτῶν ὀγδοήκοντα τεσσάρων, ἣ οὐκ ἀφίστατο τοῦ ἱεροῦ νηστείαις καὶ δεήσεσιν λατρεύουσα νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν.

records.literal_gloss: And was Anna a prophetess, daughter of Phanuel, of tribe of Asher; she having advanced in days many, having lived with a husband years seven from the virginity of her, \v 37 and she a widow until years eighty-four, who not departed from the temple, with fastings and prayers serving night and day.

en.L: And there was Anna, a prophetess, daughter of Phanuel, of [the] tribe of Asher. She was advanced in many days, having lived with a husband seven years from her virginity, \v 37 and she [was] a widow up to eighty-four years. She did not leave the temple, serving with fastings and prayers night and day.
en.B: A prophet was there too, Anna, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was very old. She had married as a young woman and lived with her husband seven years, \v 37 and she had been a widow ever since; she was now eighty-four. She never left the temple, but served God night and day with fasting and prayer.
en.R: A woman named Anna was also at the temple. She was a prophet, the daughter of Phanuel, from the tribe of Asher. She was very old. She had been married for seven years, and then her husband died. \v 37 She was now eighty-four years old. She stayed at the temple all the time. Day and night she worshiped God by fasting and praying.

es.L: Y había una profetisa, Ana, hija de Fanuel, de [la] tribu de Aser. Ella había avanzado en muchos días, tras vivir con un esposo siete años desde su doncellez, \v 37 y ella [era] viuda hasta [los] ochenta y cuatro años. No dejaba el templo, sirviendo [a Dios] con ayunos y súplicas noche y día.
es.B: Estaba allí también una profetisa, Ana, hija de Fanuel, de la tribu de Aser. Era ya muy anciana. Se había casado de joven y vivió siete años con su marido, \v 37 y desde entonces había quedado viuda; ahora tenía ochenta y cuatro años. Nunca salía del templo, sino que adoraba a Dios ayunando y orando día y noche.
es.R: En el templo estaba también una mujer llamada Ana. Era profetisa, hija de Fanuel, de la tribu de Aser. Era muy anciana. Había estado casada siete años, y luego su esposo murió. \v 37 Ahora tenía ochenta y cuatro años. Se quedaba en el templo todo el tiempo. Día y noche adoraba a Dios ayunando y orando.

fr.L: Et il y avait Anne, une prophétesse, fille de Phanuel, de la tribu d’Aser. Elle était d’un âge très avancé, ayant vécu avec un mari sept ans depuis sa virginité, \v 37 et elle [était] veuve jusqu’à quatre-vingt-quatre ans. Elle ne s’éloignait pas du temple, servant nuit et jour par des jeûnes et des prières.
fr.B: Il y avait là aussi une prophétesse, Anne, fille de Phanuel, de la tribu d’Aser. Elle était très âgée. Mariée toute jeune, elle avait vécu sept ans avec son mari, \v 37 puis elle était restée veuve ; elle avait maintenant quatre-vingt-quatre ans. Elle ne quittait jamais le temple, mais servait Dieu nuit et jour par le jeûne et la prière.
fr.R: Une femme appelée Anne se trouvait aussi au temple. C’était une prophétesse, la fille de Phanuel, de la tribu d’Aser. Elle était très âgée. Elle avait été mariée pendant sept ans, puis son mari était mort. \v 37 Elle avait maintenant quatre-vingt-quatre ans. Elle restait au temple tout le temps. Jour et nuit, elle adorait Dieu en jeûnant et en priant.

sw.L: Na palikuwa na Ana, nabii wa kike, binti wa Fanueli, kutoka kabila la Asheri. Huyu alikuwa amesonga mbele sana katika siku nyingi, baada ya kukaa na mume kwa miaka saba tangu usichana wake, \v 37 naye [alikuwa] mjane mpaka miaka themanini na minne. Hakuwa akiondoka hekaluni, akitumika kwa mifungo na maombi usiku na mchana.
sw.B: Pia palikuwa na nabii wa kike, Ana binti wa Fanueli, wa kabila la Asheri. Alikuwa mzee sana. Aliolewa akiwa msichana, akaishi na mumewe miaka saba, \v 37 na tangu hapo alikuwa mjane; sasa alikuwa na miaka themanini na minne. Hakuwahi kuondoka hekaluni, bali alimtumikia Mungu mchana na usiku kwa kufunga na kuomba.
sw.R: Mwanamke mmoja aitwaye Ana pia alikuwa hekaluni. Alikuwa nabii, binti wa Fanueli, wa kabila la Asheri. Alikuwa mzee sana. Alikuwa ameolewa kwa miaka saba, kisha mumewe akafa. \v 37 Sasa alikuwa na umri wa miaka themanini na minne. Alikaa hekaluni wakati wote. Mchana na usiku alimwabudu Mungu kwa kufunga na kuomba.

decisions.choice: a widow until eighty-four: she was now eighty-four years old
alternatives: she had been a widow for eighty-four years, and so was over one hundred
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean she had reached the age of eighty-four, or that she had been a widow for eighty-four years. The second would make her about a hundred and five, like Judith, who lived as a widow to that age (Judith 16:22-23). Both readings are possible.

decisions.choice: the tribe of Asher: one of the northern tribes
decisions.reason: Asher was one of the ten tribes of the north, scattered by Assyria. Some families kept their tribal records. Anna's presence shows that the hope is for all Israel.

decisions.choice: she did not leave the temple: she was there constantly
decisions.reason: The phrase means she was always at worship. Luke says the same of the disciples (24:53).

decisions.choice: serving: worshiping God
decisions.reason: The verb of 1:74: the service of worship. Her fasting and prayer are that worship.

decisions.choice: prophetess: a woman who speaks for God
decisions.reason: Women prophets in Scripture include Miriam, Deborah and Huldah (Exodus 15:20; Judges 4:4; 2 Kings 22:14); Acts tells of Philip's daughters (Acts 21:9).

decisions.choice: a prophet
decisions.reason: "Prophet" is the modern English word for a man or a woman. Literal keeps the feminine form.

decisions.choice: had married as a young woman
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the phrase means.

decisions.choice: profetisa
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable say "prophet" because "prophetess" sounds dated in English. Spanish "profetisa" is the ordinary word for a woman prophet and is kept at every level (meaning decision m5).

decisions.choice: une prophétesse at every level
decisions.reason: English Balanced and Readable say "prophet", the modern English word for a man or a woman. French marks gender on the noun; "prophétesse" is the usual feminine and carries no lesser sense, while "une prophète" is still rare.

source.text: καὶ αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐπιστᾶσα ἀνθωμολογεῖτο τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἐλάλει περὶ αὐτοῦ πᾶσιν τοῖς προσδεχομένοις λύτρωσιν Ἰερουσαλήμ.

records.literal_gloss: And at that very hour having come up she was giving thanks to the God and was speaking concerning him to all the [ones] waiting for redemption of Jerusalem.

en.L: And coming up at that very hour, she was giving thanks to God and speaking about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to all who were waiting for [the] redemption of Jerusalem.
en.B: She came up just then, gave thanks to God, and went on speaking about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to everyone who was waiting for God to set Jerusalem free.
en.R: She came up to Mary and Joseph at that moment. She thanked God and told everyone about the child. She spoke to all the people who were waiting for God to rescue Jerusalem.

es.L: Y llegando en ese mismo momento, daba gracias a Dios y hablaba de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a todos los que aguardaban [la] redención de Jerusalén.
es.B: Ella llegó en ese momento, dio gracias a Dios y se puso a hablar de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a todos los que esperaban que Dios liberara a Jerusalén.
es.R: En ese momento se acercó a María y a José. Dio gracias a Dios y habló del niño a todos. Les habló a todas las personas que esperaban que Dios rescatara a Jerusalén.

fr.L: Et, survenant à cette heure même, elle rendait grâce à Dieu et parlait de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} à tous ceux qui attendaient la rédemption de Jérusalem.
fr.B: Elle arriva à ce moment même, rendit grâce à Dieu et ne cessa de parler de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} à tous ceux qui attendaient que Dieu libère Jérusalem.
fr.R: À ce moment-là, elle s’est approchée de Marie et Joseph. Elle a remercié Dieu, et elle a parlé de l’enfant à tout le monde. Elle en a parlé à tous ceux qui attendaient que Dieu vienne délivrer Jérusalem.

sw.L: Na katika saa hiyo hiyo, akisogea karibu, alianza kumshukuru Mungu na kuzungumza kuhusu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kwa wote waliosubiri ukombozi wa Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Wakati huo huo alifika, akamshukuru Mungu, akaendelea kuwaeleza habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} wote waliokuwa wakisubiri Mungu aikomboe Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Wakati huo alikuja karibu na Mariamu na Yusufu. Akamshukuru Mungu, akawaambia watu wote habari za mtoto huyo. Aliwaeleza wote waliokuwa wakingoja Mungu aiokoe Yerusalemu.

decisions.choice: the redemption of Jerusalem: God's setting free of his people and city
decisions.reason: Like "the consolation of Israel" (2:25), this is the hope of Isaiah 52:9: "The LORD has comforted his people, he has redeemed Jerusalem." Zechariah used the same noun in 1:68.

decisions.choice: was speaking about him: she kept telling people about the child
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense shows that she went on doing it.

decisions.choice: waiting for God to set Jerusalem free (B); to rescue Jerusalem (R)
alternatives: waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God and say what redemption is.

source.text: Καὶ ὡς ἐτέλεσαν πάντα τὰ κατὰ τὸν νόμον κυρίου, ἐπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν εἰς πόλιν ἑαυτῶν Ναζαρέθ.

records.literal_gloss: And when they completed all the things according to the law of [the] Lord, they returned to the Galilee to city of themselves Nazareth.

en.L: And when they had completed everything according to the law of [the] Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own town Nazareth.
en.B: When they had carried out everything the law of the Lord required, they went back to Galilee, to Nazareth, their own town.
en.R: When Joseph and Mary had done everything the Lord's law required, they went home to their own town of Nazareth in Galilee.

es.L: Y cuando acabaron todas las cosas conforme a la ley del Señor, regresaron a Galilea, a la ciudad de ellos, Nazaret.
es.B: Cuando terminaron de hacer todo lo que la ley del Señor pedía, se volvieron a Galilea, a Nazaret, su propio pueblo.
es.R: Cuando José y María terminaron de hacer todo lo que mandaba la ley del Señor, volvieron a casa, a su pueblo de Nazaret, en Galilea.

fr.L: Et quand ils eurent tout accompli selon la Loi du Seigneur, ils retournèrent en Galilée, dans leur ville, Nazareth.
fr.B: Quand ils eurent accompli tout ce que demandait la Loi du Seigneur, ils retournèrent en Galilée, à Nazareth, leur ville.
fr.R: Après avoir fait tout ce que la Loi du Seigneur demandait, Joseph et Marie sont rentrés chez eux, dans leur ville de Nazareth, en Galilée.

sw.L: Na walipomaliza mambo yote kulingana na sheria ya Bwana, walirudi Galilaya, katika mji wao wenyewe, Nazareti.
sw.B: Walipokwisha kufanya kila kitu ambacho sheria ya Bwana iliagiza, walirudi Galilaya, Nazareti, mji wao.
sw.R: Yusufu na Mariamu walipomaliza kufanya kila kitu ambacho sheria ya Bwana iliagiza, walirudi nyumbani katika mji wao wa Nazareti huko Galilaya.

decisions.choice: they returned to Galilee: Luke goes straight from the temple to Nazareth
alternatives: they went home the same day
decisions.reason: Luke does not tell of the magi or the flight to Egypt (Matthew 2:1-23). He closes this part of the story with the family's return home, without saying how much time passed.

source.text: Τὸ δὲ παιδίον ηὔξανεν καὶ ἐκραταιοῦτο πληρούμενον σοφίᾳ, καὶ χάρις θεοῦ ἦν ἐπ’ αὐτό.

records.literal_gloss: The and child was growing and was becoming strong being filled with wisdom, and grace of God was upon him.

en.L: And the child kept growing and becoming strong, being filled with wisdom, and [the] grace of God was upon {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The child kept growing and gaining strength. He was filled with wisdom, and the grace of God rested on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus grew and became strong. He became very wise, and God's grace was on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y el niño iba creciendo y haciéndose fuerte, llenándose de sabiduría, y [la] gracia de Dios estaba sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: El niño seguía creciendo y cobrando fuerzas. Estaba lleno de sabiduría, y la gracia de Dios reposaba sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Jesús creció y se hizo fuerte. Llegó a ser muy sabio, y la gracia de Dios estaba sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Et l’enfant grandissait et devenait fort, se remplissant de sagesse, et la grâce de Dieu était sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: L’enfant continuait de grandir et de prendre des forces. Il était plein de sagesse, et la grâce de Dieu reposait sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Jésus a grandi et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est devenu fort. Il est devenu très sage, et la grâce de Dieu était sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Naye mtoto alikuwa akikua na kuimarika, akijazwa hekima, na neema ya Mungu ilikaa juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Mtoto akaendelea kukua na kupata nguvu. Alijaa hekima, na neema ya Mungu ilikaa juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Yesu alikua, akawa na nguvu. Akawa na hekima nyingi, na neema ya Mungu ilikuwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.

decisions.choice: became strong, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: became strong in spirit, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "in spirit", from what is said of John in 1:80. Early manuscripts do not have it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: being filled with wisdom: wisdom growing in him as he grew
alternatives: already full of wisdom from the start
decisions.reason: The present participle describes a process. Jesus grows as a real child grows (compare 2:52).

decisions.choice: the grace of God was upon him: God's favor rested on him
decisions.reason: Grace here is God's kindness and favor toward the child, as with Samuel (1 Samuel 2:26).

source.text: Καὶ ἐπορεύοντο οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ κατ’ ἔτος εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ τῇ ἑορτῇ τοῦ πάσχα.

records.literal_gloss: And were going the parents of him by year to Jerusalem at the feast of the Passover.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} parents went every year to Jerusalem at the feast of the Passover.
en.B: Year by year {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} parents used to go up to Jerusalem for the feast of Passover.
en.R: Each year Jesus's parents traveled to Jerusalem to celebrate Passover.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} padres viajaban cada año a Jerusalén para la fiesta de la Pascua.
es.B: Año tras año, {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} padres subían a Jerusalén para la fiesta de la Pascua.
es.R: Cada año, los padres de Jesús viajaban a Jerusalén para celebrar la Pascua.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} parents allaient chaque année à Jérusalem pour la fête de la Pâque.
fr.B: Chaque année, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} parents montaient à Jérusalem pour la fête de la Pâque.
fr.R: Chaque année, les parents de Jésus allaient à Jérusalem pour fêter la Pâque.

sw.L: Na wazazi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa wakienda Yerusalemu kila mwaka katika sikukuu ya Pasaka.
sw.B: Kila mwaka wazazi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa na desturi ya kupanda Yerusalemu kwa ajili ya sikukuu ya Pasaka.
sw.R: Kila mwaka wazazi wa Yesu walisafiri kwenda Yerusalemu kusherehekea Pasaka.

decisions.choice: the feast of the Passover: the spring festival remembering the exodus from Egypt
decisions.reason: Jewish men were to go to Jerusalem for three feasts each year: Passover, Weeks and Booths (Deuteronomy 16:16). Many who lived far away went only for Passover. The feast with the week of Unleavened Bread lasted eight days.

decisions.choice: were going: they used to go, every year
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense with "every year" shows a habit. The parents are faithful to the law.

decisions.choice: la Pâque
decisions.reason: As the term sheet (style guide 9) has it: "la Pâque" is the Jewish festival; "Pâques" is the Christian feast of the resurrection.

source.text: καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἐτῶν δώδεκα, ἀναβαινόντων αὐτῶν κατὰ τὸ ἔθος τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ τελειωσάντων τὰς ἡμέρας, ἐν τῷ ὑποστρέφειν αὐτοὺς ὑπέμεινεν Ἰησοῦς ὁ παῖς ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ, καὶ οὐκ ἔγνωσαν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And when he was years twelve, going up them according to the custom of the feast \v 43 and having completed the days, in the returning them remained Jesus the boy in Jerusalem, and not knew the parents of him.

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was twelve years [old], as they went up according to the custom of the feast \v 43 and had completed the days, while they were returning, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} parents did not know [it].
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was twelve, they went up as the custom of the feast was. \v 43 After the days of the feast were over, as they set off for home, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem without {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} parents knowing.
en.R: When Jesus was twelve years old, they went to the festival as usual. \v 43 When the festival was over, Joseph and Mary started back home. But Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem, and they did not know it.

es.L: Y cuando tuvo doce años, subiendo ellos según la costumbre de la fiesta \v 43 y habiendo completado los días, al regresar ellos, el muchacho Jesús permaneció en Jerusalén, y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} padres no [lo] supieron.
es.B: Cuando cumplió doce años, subieron como era costumbre en la fiesta. \v 43 Terminados los días de la fiesta, al emprender el regreso, el muchacho Jesús se quedó en Jerusalén sin que {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} padres se dieran cuenta.
es.R: Cuando Jesús tenía doce años, fueron a la fiesta como siempre. \v 43 Al terminar la fiesta, José y María emprendieron el camino de regreso a casa. Pero Jesús se quedó en Jerusalén, y ellos no lo sabían.

fr.L: Et quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} eut douze ans, comme ils montaient selon la coutume de la fête \v 43 et qu’ils en avaient achevé les jours, pendant qu’ils s’en retournaient, l’enfant Jésus resta à Jérusalem, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} parents ne [le] surent pas.
fr.B: Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} eut douze ans, ils y montèrent selon la coutume de la fête. \v 43 Une fois les jours de fête terminés, alors qu’ils reprenaient le chemin du retour, le jeune Jésus resta à Jérusalem sans que {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} parents le sachent.
fr.R: Quand Jésus a eu douze ans, ils sont allés à la fête comme d’habitude. \v 43 Après la fête, Joseph et Marie ont repris le chemin de la maison. Mais Jésus est resté à Jérusalem, et ils ne le savaient pas.

sw.L: Na alipokuwa [na umri wa] miaka kumi na miwili, wao wakipanda kwa mujibu wa desturi ya sikukuu \v 43 na wakiisha kumaliza siku [zile], walipokuwa wakirudi, kijana Yesu alibaki Yerusalemu, na wazazi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} hawakujua.
sw.B: Alipokuwa na miaka kumi na miwili, walipanda kama ilivyokuwa desturi ya sikukuu. \v 43 Siku za sikukuu zilipokwisha, walianza safari ya kurudi nyumbani, lakini kijana Yesu alibaki Yerusalemu bila wazazi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kujua.
sw.R: Yesu alipokuwa na umri wa miaka kumi na miwili, walikwenda kwenye sikukuu kama kawaida. \v 43 Sikukuu ilipokwisha, Yusufu na Mariamu walianza safari ya kurudi nyumbani. Lakini Yesu alibaki Yerusalemu, nao hawakujua.

decisions.choice: twelve years old: on the edge of adult religious duty
alternatives: the age of a bar mitzvah
decisions.reason: Later Jewish custom made a boy responsible for the commandments at thirteen. At twelve Jesus may have been preparing for that step. The bar mitzvah ceremony itself is later than the New Testament.

decisions.choice: the boy: a child, here a boy of twelve
decisions.reason: The word can mean a child or a servant. Luke calls Jesus a child (2:40) and now a boy, as he grows.

decisions.choice: his parents, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Joseph and his mother, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: As in 2:33, many later manuscripts avoid calling Joseph his parent. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

source.text: νομίσαντες δὲ αὐτὸν εἶναι ἐν τῇ συνοδίᾳ ἦλθον ἡμέρας ὁδὸν καὶ ἀνεζήτουν αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς συγγενεῦσιν καὶ τοῖς γνωστοῖς, καὶ μὴ εὑρόντες ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἀναζητοῦντες αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Having supposed and him to be in the caravan they went of a day a journey and were searching for him among the relatives and the acquaintances, \v 45 and not having found they returned to Jerusalem searching for him.

en.L: But supposing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to be in the caravan, they went a day's journey, and they were searching for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} among the relatives and acquaintances, \v 45 and not finding [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], they returned to Jerusalem, searching for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Thinking {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was with the others on the road, they travelled for a whole day; then they began hunting for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} among their relatives and the people they knew. \v 45 Not finding {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they turned back to Jerusalem, still searching for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: They thought {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was with the large group of people traveling with them. After a whole day of travel, they began to look for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} among their relatives and friends. \v 45 They could not find {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so they went back to Jerusalem to look for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} there.

es.L: Pero creyendo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} iba en la caravana, recorrieron una jornada de camino, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} buscaban entre los parientes y los conocidos, \v 45 y al no dar con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, regresaron a Jerusalén en busca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Pensando que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} iba con los demás en el camino, viajaron un día entero; luego {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} empezaron a buscar entre sus parientes y la gente conocida. \v 45 Como no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} encontraban, volvieron a Jerusalén y allí {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} seguían buscando.
es.R: Pensaban que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} venía con el grupo grande de gente que viajaba con ellos. Después de un día entero de camino, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} empezaron a buscar entre sus parientes y amigos. \v 45 No {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} pudieron encontrar, así que volvieron a Jerusalén y allí {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} buscaron.

fr.L: Mais, supposant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était dans la caravane, ils parcoururent le chemin d’une journée, et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} cherchaient parmi la parenté et les connaissances, \v 45 et, ne [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] trouvant pas, ils retournèrent à Jérusalem en {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} cherchant.
fr.B: Pensant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était avec les autres voyageurs, ils marchèrent toute une journée ; puis ils se mirent à {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} chercher parmi leur famille et les gens qu’ils connaissaient. \v 45 Comme ils ne {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} trouvaient pas, ils retournèrent à Jérusalem, en continuant à {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} chercher.
fr.R: Ils pensaient qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était dans le grand groupe de gens qui voyageaient avec eux. Après une journée de marche, ils ont commencé à {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} chercher parmi leur famille et leurs amis. \v 45 Ils ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont pas trouvé, alors ils sont retournés à Jérusalem pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} chercher là-bas.

sw.L: Lakini wakifikiri {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} yuko katika kundi la wasafiri, walisafiri safari ya siku moja, na wakawa wakimtafuta miongoni mwa jamaa na watu waliofahamiana nao, \v 45 na wasipompata, walirejea Yerusalemu wakimtafutatafuta.
sw.B: Wakidhani kwamba alikuwa pamoja na wenzao njiani, walisafiri siku nzima; kisha wakaanza kumtafuta kati ya jamaa zao na watu waliowajua. \v 45 Wasipompata, walirudi Yerusalemu, wakiendelea kumtafuta.
sw.R: Walidhani yuko pamoja na kundi kubwa la watu waliokuwa wakisafiri pamoja nao. Baada ya kusafiri siku nzima, walianza kumtafuta kati ya jamaa na rafiki zao. \v 45 Hawakuweza kumpata, kwa hiyo walirudi Yerusalemu kumtafuta huko.

decisions.choice: the caravan: a large group of relatives and neighbors travelling together
decisions.reason: Pilgrims from Galilee travelled to the feasts in large groups for safety. A boy of twelve could walk with relatives or friends without his parents' notice.

source.text: καὶ ἐγένετο μετὰ ἡμέρας τρεῖς εὗρον αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καθεζόμενον ἐν μέσῳ τῶν διδασκάλων καὶ ἀκούοντα αὐτῶν καὶ ἐπερωτῶντα αὐτούς·

records.literal_gloss: And it came to pass after days three they found him in the temple sitting in [the] middle of the teachers and hearing them and questioning them;

en.L: And it happened, after three days they found {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the temple, sitting in [the] middle of the teachers, both listening to them and asking them questions.
en.B: Three days later they found {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the temple, seated among the teachers, listening to them and putting questions to them.
en.R: After three days they found {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the temple courtyard. He was sitting with the teachers of God's law, listening to them and asking them questions.

es.L: Y sucedió que después de tres días {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} encontraron en el templo, sentado en medio de los maestros, escuchándolos y haciéndoles preguntas.
es.B: Al cabo de tres días {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} encontraron en el templo, sentado entre los maestros, escuchándolos y planteándoles preguntas.
es.R: Después de tres días {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} encontraron en el patio del templo. Estaba sentado con los maestros de la ley de Dios, escuchándolos y haciéndoles preguntas.

fr.L: Et il arriva qu’au bout de trois jours ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} trouvèrent dans le temple, assis au milieu des maîtres, les écoutant et les interrogeant.
fr.B: Trois jours plus tard, ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} trouvèrent dans la cour du temple, assis parmi les maîtres ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les écoutait et leur posait des questions.
fr.R: Au bout de trois jours, ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont trouvé dans la cour du temple. Il était assis avec les maîtres qui enseignaient la Loi de Dieu. Il les écoutait et leur posait des questions.

sw.L: Na ilitokea, baada ya siku tatu walimpata ndani ya hekalu, akiwa ameketi katikati ya walimu, akiwasikia na pia akiwahoji.
sw.B: Siku tatu baadaye walimpata hekaluni, akiwa ameketi pamoja na walimu, akiwasikiliza huku akiwauliza maswali.
sw.R: Baada ya siku tatu walimpata katika ua wa hekalu. Aliketi na walimu wa sheria ya Mungu. Alikuwa akiwasikiliza na kuwauliza maswali.

decisions.choice: after three days: counting from when they left Jerusalem
alternatives: three days of searching in the city
decisions.reason: One day out, one day back, and on the third day they found him, by the usual Jewish way of counting.

decisions.choice: sitting among the teachers: teachers of the law met with pupils in the temple courts
decisions.reason: Pupils sat with their teachers, listening and asking questions. Jesus behaves as a pupil, but his understanding astonishes them (2:47).

decisions.choice: les maîtres
decisions.reason: "Les docteurs" is the traditional word but now means physicians or holders of a doctorate; "les enseignants" sounds like schoolteachers. "Les maîtres" is a teacher with pupils, as in the temple courts (m2); Readable adds what they taught, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ἐξίσταντο δὲ πάντες οἱ ἀκούοντες αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῇ συνέσει καὶ ταῖς ἀποκρίσεσιν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Were amazed then all the [ones] hearing him at the understanding and the answers of him.

en.L: And all who heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} were amazed at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} understanding and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} answers.
en.B: Everyone who heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} was astounded at how much {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} understood and at the answers {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave.
en.R: All the people who heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} were amazed. He understood so much, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave such good answers!

es.L: Y estaban atónitos todos los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} escuchaban, por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} entendimiento y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} respuestas.
es.B: Todos los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} oían quedaban asombrados de lo mucho que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} entendía y de las respuestas que daba.
es.R: Toda la gente que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} oía estaba asombrada. ¡Entendía tanto, y daba tan buenas respuestas!

fr.L: Et tous ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}écoutaient restaient stupéfaits devant {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} intelligence et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} réponses.
fr.B: Tous ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}entendaient étaient émerveillés de tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} comprenait et des réponses qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donnait.
fr.R: Tous les gens qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}entendaient étaient très étonnés. Il comprenait tant de choses, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donnait de si bonnes réponses !

sw.L: Na wote waliomsikia walishangaa kwa ufahamu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na majibu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Kila aliyemsikia alishangazwa jinsi alivyoelewa mambo mengi na majibu aliyotoa.
sw.R: Watu wote waliomsikia walishangaa. Alielewa mambo mengi sana, na majibu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yalikuwa mazuri mno!

decisions.choice: understanding: insight into the meaning of things
decisions.reason: The noun is used of wisdom that grasps how things fit together. It goes with the wisdom of 2:40 and 2:52.

source.text: καὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐξεπλάγησαν, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ· Τέκνον, τί ἐποίησας ἡμῖν οὕτως;

records.literal_gloss: And having seen him they were astonished, and said to him the mother of him, Child, why did you do to us thus?

en.L: And when they saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they were astonished, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Child, why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} done this to us?
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} parents saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they were stunned, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "My child, why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} treated us like this?
en.R: When Joseph and Mary saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they were shocked. His mother said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Son, why did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do this to us?

es.L: Y cuando {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vieron, quedaron atónitos, y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Hijo, ¿por qué nos hiciste esto?
es.B: Cuando {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} padres {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vieron, se quedaron pasmados, y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Hijo mío, ¿por qué nos has tratado así?
es.R: Cuando José y María {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vieron, se sorprendieron muchísimo. Su madre {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Hijo, ¿por qué nos hiciste esto?

fr.L: Et en {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voyant, ils furent frappés d’étonnement, et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Enfant, pourquoi nous as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fait cela ?
fr.B: Quand {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} parents {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} virent, ils furent bouleversés, et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Mon enfant, pourquoi nous as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} traités ainsi ?
fr.R: Quand Joseph et Marie {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont vu, ils ont été bouleversés. Sa mère {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a dit : « Mon fils, pourquoi nous as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fait cela ?

sw.L: Na walipomwona, walishangaa sana, na mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} akamwambia, "Mwanangu, kwa nini umetufanyia hivi?
sw.B: Wazazi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walipomwona walipigwa na bumbuazi, na mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} akamwambia, "Mwanangu, kwa nini umetutendea namna hii?
sw.R: Yusufu na Mariamu walipomwona, walishtuka sana. Mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} akamwambia, "Mwanangu, kwa nini umetufanyia hivi?

decisions.choice: astonished: overwhelmed with surprise
decisions.reason: The verb means to be struck with amazement, at finding him there and at what they saw.

decisions.choice: My child (B); Son (R)
decisions.reason: A mother's tender word to her child. "Child" alone sounds cold in English.

decisions.choice: his parents (B); Joseph and Mary (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "they" are, since the last subject was the teachers.

decisions.choice: Hijo (L, R); Hijo mío (B)
decisions.reason: The word is "child" as one's own child. A Spanish mother says "hijo"; "niño" would sound distant, so Literal says "Hijo" where the English Literal has "Child".

source.text: ἰδοὺ ὁ πατήρ σου καὶ ἐγὼ ὀδυνώμενοι ἐζητοῦμέν σε.

records.literal_gloss: Behold the father of you and I being in anguish were seeking you.

en.L: Look, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} father and I have been searching for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in anguish."
en.B: Your father and I have been looking for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, sick with worry."
en.R: Your father and I have been very worried. We have been looking everywhere for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"

es.L: Mira, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} padre y yo, angustiados, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} buscábamos».
es.B: Tu padre y yo {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} hemos estado buscando, muertos de preocupación».
es.R: Tu padre y yo hemos estado muy preocupados. ¡Hemos estado buscándote por todas partes!».

fr.L: Voici, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} père et moi, angoissés, nous {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} cherchions. »
fr.B: Ton père et moi, nous {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} cherchions, fous d’inquiétude. »
fr.R: Ton père et moi, nous étions très inquiets. Nous {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}avons cherché partout ! »

sw.L: Tazama, baba {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} nami tumekuwa tukikutafuta kwa uchungu."
sw.B: Baba {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} nami tumekuwa tukikutafuta, tukiwa na wasiwasi mwingi."
sw.R: Baba {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} nami tumekuwa na wasiwasi mwingi. Tumekutafuta kila mahali!"

decisions.choice: in anguish: in great distress
decisions.reason: The verb means to suffer pain or grief (16:24-25; Acts 20:38).

decisions.choice: your father: Joseph
decisions.reason: Mary means Joseph. Jesus's answer turns the word to God, "my Father" (2:49).

decisions.choice: the quotation opened in 2:48a closes at the end of this sentence
decisions.reason: Both sentences are Mary's words to Jesus, so French closes the quotation marks here, as the English does.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τί ὅτι ἐζητεῖτέ με;

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, Why that you were seeking me?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Why [is it] that you were searching for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?
en.B: He said to them, "Why were you looking for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?
en.R: Jesus said to them, "Why did you have to look for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les dijo: «¿Por qué [es] que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:buscaban|buscabais}}?
es.B: Él les respondió: «¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:buscaban|buscabais}}?
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:tuvieron|tuvisteis}} que buscar?

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Pourquoi [est-ce] que vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} cherchiez ?
fr.B: Il leur dit : « Pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} cherchiez-vous ?
fr.R: Jésus leur a répondu : « Pourquoi avez-vous dû {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} chercher ?

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, "Ni kwa sababu gani mlikuwa mkinitafuta?
sw.B: Akawaambia, "Kwa nini mlikuwa mkinitafuta?
sw.R: Yesu akawaambia, "Kwa nini mlihitaji kunitafuta?

decisions.choice: why were you searching for me: not a rebuke, but surprise that they did not know where to find him
decisions.reason: The next question explains: they should have known where he would be. These are Jesus's first words in Luke.

source.text: οὐκ ᾔδειτε ὅτι ἐν τοῖς τοῦ πατρός μου δεῖ εἶναί με;

records.literal_gloss: Not did you know that in the [things] of the Father of me it is necessary to be me?

en.L: Did you not know that I must be in the [house] of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father?"
en.B: Did you not know that I must be in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father's house?"
en.R: Did you not know that I must be in the house of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father?"

es.L: ¿No {{plural_you:sabían|sabíais}} que yo debo estar en la [casa] de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre?».
es.B: ¿No {{plural_you:sabían|sabíais}} que yo tenía que estar en la casa de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre?».
es.R: ¿No {{plural_you:sabían|sabíais}} que yo debo estar en la casa de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre?».

fr.L: Ne saviez-vous pas que je dois être chez {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père ? »
fr.B: Ne saviez-vous pas qu’il {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} fallait être chez {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père ? »
fr.R: Ne saviez-vous pas que je dois être dans la maison de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père ? »

sw.L: Je, hamkujua kwamba ni lazima {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niwe katika [nyumba] ya Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}?"
sw.B: Hamkujua kwamba sina budi kuwa katika nyumba ya Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}?"
sw.R: Hamkujua kwamba lazima niwe katika nyumba ya Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}?"

decisions.choice: in my Father's house: in the temple
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "in the things of my Father". In similar Greek phrases this usually means someone's house, and they found him in the temple, so "house" fits best. "About my Father's business" is also possible.

decisions.choice: my Father: God
decisions.reason: Mary said "your father" of Joseph (2:48); Jesus calls God "my Father". He knows who he is, as the angel said (1:32, 35).

decisions.choice: must: it is necessary, by God's will
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word for what must happen in God's plan (4:43; 9:22; 24:7, 26, 44).

decisions.choice: chez mon Père (L, B); dans la maison de mon Père (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "in the [things] of my Father" with no noun, and m1 reads it as the temple. French "chez" means "at the home of" without naming the house, so Literal and Balanced can say it as briefly as the Greek, with no bracket. Readable names the house.

source.text: καὶ αὐτοὶ οὐ συνῆκαν τὸ ῥῆμα ὃ ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And they not understood the word which he spoke to them.

en.L: And they did not understand the word that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to them.
en.B: But they did not grasp what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} meant.
en.R: But they did not understand what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was telling them.

es.L: Y ellos no entendieron la palabra que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les habló.
es.B: Pero ellos no comprendieron lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quería decir.
es.R: Pero ellos no entendieron lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les estaba diciendo.

fr.L: Et eux ne comprirent pas la parole qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur adressa.
fr.B: Mais ils ne saisirent pas ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} voulait dire.
fr.R: Mais ils n’ont pas compris ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur disait.

sw.L: Nao wenyewe hawakulielewa neno ambalo {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliwaambia.
sw.B: Lakini hawakuelewa maana ya maneno {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Lakini hawakuelewa alichokuwa akiwaambia.

decisions.choice: they did not understand: even his parents did not yet see who he was
decisions.reason: Mary has heard much about her son, but she does not yet understand all of it. Later the disciples too fail to understand (9:45; 18:34).

source.text: καὶ κατέβη μετ’ αὐτῶν καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς Ναζαρὲθ, καὶ ἦν ὑποτασσόμενος αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was being subject to them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went down with them and came to Nazareth, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was subject to them.
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went back down with them to Nazareth, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lived under their authority.
en.R: Then Jesus went back to Nazareth with them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} obeyed them.

es.L: Y bajó con ellos y llegó a Nazaret, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} vivía sujeto a ellos.
es.B: Así que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} regresó con ellos a Nazaret, y vivió bajo la autoridad de ellos.
es.R: Luego Jesús volvió a Nazaret con ellos, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los obedecía.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} descendit avec eux et vint à Nazareth, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur était soumis.
fr.B: Il redescendit donc avec eux à Nazareth, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vivait sous leur autorité.
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus est retourné à Nazareth avec eux, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur obéissait.

sw.L: Na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alishuka pamoja nao, akaenda Nazareti, na alikuwa akijitiisha kwao.
sw.B: Basi alishuka pamoja nao hadi Nazareti, akaishi chini ya mamlaka yao.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu alirudi Nazareti pamoja nao, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} aliwatii.

decisions.choice: was subject to them: he went on obeying his parents
decisions.reason: The periphrastic imperfect shows a continuing way of life. The one who must be in his Father's house also keeps the commandment to honor father and mother (Exodus 20:12).

source.text: καὶ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ διετήρει πάντα τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτῆς.

records.literal_gloss: And the mother of him was keeping all the words in the heart of her.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother kept all the words in her heart.
en.B: His mother kept all these things safe in her heart.
en.R: His mother kept thinking about all these things.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre conservaba todas las palabras en su corazón.
es.B: Su madre guardaba con cuidado todas estas cosas en su corazón.
es.R: Su madre seguía pensando en todas estas cosas.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère gardait toutes ces paroles dans son cœur.
fr.B: Sa mère conservait précieusement tout cela dans son cœur.
fr.R: Sa mère continuait à penser à tout cela.

sw.L: Na mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} alikuwa akiyahifadhi maneno yote ndani ya moyo wake.
sw.B: Mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} aliyatunza mambo haya yote moyoni mwake.
sw.R: Mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} aliendelea kuyafikiria mambo hayo yote.

decisions.choice: kept all the words in her heart: she held on to these events and thought about them
decisions.reason: As in 2:19. Luke may be pointing to Mary as a source of these memories.

decisions.choice: all the words, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: all these words, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "these". The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: these things
decisions.reason: As in 2:19, the noun means the events and what was said about them.

source.text: Καὶ Ἰησοῦς προέκοπτεν σοφίᾳ καὶ ἡλικίᾳ καὶ χάριτι παρὰ θεῷ καὶ ἀνθρώποις.

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus was advancing in wisdom and stature and favor with God and men.

en.L: And Jesus kept advancing in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and {{gender:people|men}}.
en.B: And Jesus advanced in wisdom and in stature, and in favor with God and with {{gender:people|men}}.
en.R: Jesus grew wiser and taller. God was pleased with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and so were the people who knew {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y Jesús seguía avanzando en sabiduría y estatura, y en favor ante Dios y {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}.
es.B: Y Jesús avanzaba en sabiduría y en estatura, y gozaba del favor de Dios y de {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}.
es.R: Jesús se hacía más sabio y más alto. Dios estaba contento con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y también la gente que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} conocía.

fr.L: Et Jésus progressait en sagesse et en stature, et en faveur auprès de Dieu et des {{gender:humains|hommes}}.
fr.B: Et Jésus grandissait en sagesse et en taille, et gagnait la faveur de Dieu et des {{gender:humains|hommes}}.
fr.R: Jésus est devenu plus sage et plus grand. Dieu était content de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et les gens qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} connaissaient aussi.

sw.L: Na Yesu alikuwa akisonga mbele katika hekima na kimo, na katika kibali kwa Mungu na kwa watu.
sw.B: Yesu aliendelea kukua katika hekima na kimo, akipata kibali kwa Mungu na kwa watu.
sw.R: Yesu alizidi kuwa na hekima na kurefuka. Mungu alipendezwa {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, na watu waliomjua pia walipendezwa {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.

decisions.choice: favor: the goodwill of God and people
alternatives: grace in the sense of saving grace
decisions.reason: The key word "grace" here means favor, as with God and people together it must. The verse echoes what is said of the boy Samuel (1 Samuel 2:26).

decisions.choice: stature: growth in body, or in age
decisions.reason: The noun can mean age or bodily height (19:3). Beside wisdom it most likely means he grew up in body; either way he grew as every child does.

decisions.choice: an echo of 1 Samuel 2:26
decisions.reason: The boy Samuel grew, and was in favor both with the LORD and with people. Luke's story of Jesus's childhood ends as Samuel's did.

decisions.choice: God was pleased with him, and so were the people who knew him
alternatives: in favor with God and people
decisions.reason: Readable says what favor with God and people means.
